speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the Ministry will consider making public the data on complaints of unfair employment practices received by the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) or the Ministry that identify the employer, specific complaint, and action taken; and (b) what considerations the Ministry has in publishing such data or keeping such data confidential.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In investigating these complaints, TAFEP would engage the employers involved, and employers are generally cooperative.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Most of the complaints arise because employers do not have a proper system to address internal grievances or are insensitive to the different needs and conditions of employees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For the former, TAFEP would help employers improve their internal practices and processes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For the latter, our priority is to resolve such complaints amicably in a way that allows both the employers and the employees to move on from the incidents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: These involve employers who are not cooperative with TAFEP or who are found to adopt unfair employment practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: To raise public awareness and prevent unfair employment practices, TAFEP develops case studies from actual cases and educates employers through focused channels, such as TAFEP's briefings and workshops, to share contextualised learnings from specific cases.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Employers can better understand and appreciate the need to adopt fair employment practices through such in-depth discussions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I think the concern here among the public is whether there is effective action taken when they make a complaint on discrimination.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Of course, I understand the Ministry and TAFEP are doing all they can on this matter.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But I suppose when many employers are not named specifically, when only case studies are made, perhaps the most erroneous are named, then perhaps, there may be the perception amongst discriminated against parties that not much is being done by the Government on this front.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: So, I would appreciate if the Minister of State could reconsider this policy of not naming, in general, employers in cases.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: One thing that I wish to assure the Member and Singaporeans in general about is that TAFEP will assess every complaint that comes in, especially those that are based on facts, and certainly, where you have a formal complaint where the employee also identifies himself, puts a specific complaint on the employer.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We will listen to both sides, the employer as well as the employee.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, to a certain sense, Members can see from the number of complaints and the number of companies that we have taken action against, it is quite substantive.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, to a certain sense, Members can see that there is action being taken.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And certainly, we have to be fair to both employees and employers to make sure that the cases are dealt with fairly.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Since the inception of TAFEP, has the number of complaints, in terms of discriminatory practices or in addition to that, increased over time?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Minister of State share the general trend of the number of complaints since the inception of TAFEP?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: As TAFEP flags out annually the kind of complaints it receives, is it possible to outline it?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: If the Minister of State cannot pinpoint a company and name a company, then perhaps the type of companies, that is, the sectors, the nature of the complaints, what kinds of discriminatory practices or unfair practices and as well as the size of the company.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And, in certain cases where the situation can be egregious, we actually name the companies.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we are not shy from naming companies.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But to name every single one, well, there are different considerations.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Two, you may end up breaching the privacy of the employers, especially if it is just one targeted.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we have to be quite careful about the kind of cases we put up.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But generally, we do contextualise and put up case studies for other companies.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But certainly, we will consider the Member's suggestion.
